judge_assessment.explanation: Every claim the judge made is true. I solved all 12 equations independently and back-substituted: 3(x+4)=21 -> 3; -2(x-5)=14 -> -2; x/3+x/6=5 -> 10; 4-2(x+3)=10 -> -6; 12(x/4+2/3)=3x+8; 3(x-2)=2(x+4) -> 14; 3x/4-2=x/2 -> 8; (1/2)(6x-8)=11 -> 5; 7-3(2x-5)=22-6x; (2/3)(x+6)=(1/2)(x+2)+5 -> 12; (x+3)/2-(x-5)/4=5 -> 9; (2/5)(10x-15)=3(x-1)+4 -> 7. The worked pattern in the directions (x/2+1/3=2(x-1) -> 14/9) is also correct, as are all three study-guide try-its (x=7, x=6, x=12). The 12 problems are visually present across 5 pages. My one disagreement is with curriculum_alignment 4/4, which the judge did not examine: verify.json tags all 12 problems '6.EE.B.7 / 7.EE.B.4', which is the standards-map.md row for 'One/two-step equations' (line 63). The prompt names the topic 'Linear equations in one variable', and references/standards-map.md line 52 carries that exact row mapped to 8.EE.C.7 - which is also the task contract's standard_refs. The answer key therefore prints 'Level: Grade 8 / Pre-Algebra' directly above a curriculum line citing grade 6-7 one-step-equation codes for a sheet whose hardest item is a difficulty-5 multi-step fractional distribution.

strengths_to_preserve: The ramp genuinely avoids a repeated skeleton: problems 5 and 9 isolate the two rewrite sub-skills on their own (multiply x/4 + 2/3 by the LCD 12; expand 7 - 3(2x - 5)) instead of burying them inside another solve, and problem 11 is the only one with a fraction bar over a whole numerator, flagged in the stem with 'keep the brackets when you multiply'.

The key attaches the specific wrong answer each targeted slip produces - x = -12 in problem 2 from not distributing the negative, and x = 19 in problem 11 from '2x + 6 - x - 5' where the minus reaches only the first term of the numerator. That converts a wrong paper into a diagnosis.

Every solution follows the same four named moves in the same order (clear fractions, distribute, collect, isolate) and most end with a substitution check, which is exactly the procedural-fluency format the prompt asked for.

root_causes.description: The standard code was chosen by matching the surface features of the problems (equations with brackets and fractions) instead of the topic row the prompt names, and nothing in the pipeline cross-checks the chosen row against the requested topic. The map was consulted - no code was invented - but the wrong row was taken, and the mis-tag then prints verbatim in the answer key's generated Curriculum block.
evidence: references/standards-map.md line 52: 'Linear equations in one variable | 8.EE.C.7' - the prompt's topic verbatim; line 63 is the row actually used, 'One/two-step equations'.
task.json standard_refs is ['8.EE.C.7']; answer_key.pdf prints '6.EE.B.7 / 7.EE.B.4 - problems 1..12' under 'Level: Grade 8 / Pre-Algebra'.

improvements.title: Tag this sheet 8.EE.C.7 and check the chosen standards row against the requested topic
improvements.proposed_change: Retag all 12 problems '8.EE.C.7'. Then make the choice checkable: have verify.py report the standards-map row title behind each code it sees, and add a step to SKILL.md requiring the author to name the standards-map row matched to the requested topic before tagging. Where the topic string appears verbatim in standards-map.md, warn when a different row's code is used.
improvements.regression_test: Add a test that runs verify.py over a fixture whose topic string matches a standards-map row exactly while its problems carry a different row's code, and assert the run reports a standards mismatch naming both row titles. It fails today (verify.py accepts any in-map code silently) and passes after the check.
improvements.expected_impact: The answer key's Curriculum block, which is the one place a parent or teacher reads the level, stops understating the content by two grade bands; standards-based reporting across the suite becomes trustworthy.
improvements.risk: Topic strings do not always match a row verbatim, so the check must warn rather than hard-fail when no exact row exists, or it will block legitimate sheets on topics the map does not name.

case_summary: A clean procedural-fluency sheet: 12 distinct equation skeletons, a worked pattern in the directions that names the four moves, and a ramp that ends with a difficulty-5 fractional distribution. I re-solved and back-substituted all 12 plus the three study-guide try-its; every value in the key, the quick-answer bank and the guide agrees. The one defect is a tagging error the judge did not look at: all 12 problems are tagged with the standards-map row for one- and two-step equations (6.EE.B.7 / 7.EE.B.4) even though the prompt names 'Linear equations in one variable', which that same file maps to 8.EE.C.7 - the code the task contract expects. The code was not invented, just taken from the wrong row, and it prints in the key's Curriculum block.
